soundness_flags.label: ass:positive-basin-mass / ass:basin-nondegeneracy / ass:jacobian-nonsingular
soundness_flags.one_line: The stated results do not use the common lower basin-mass bound, while the upper covariance and Jacobian bounds follow respectively from bounded scores plus overlap and from the derivative envelope; retain only bounds that enter a displayed uniform estimate.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:finite-tail-selection and ass:uniform-attraction-modulus
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Finite tail selection and its Cesaro modulus are assumed rather than derived for any deployed learner, including the Guo--Xu analogue.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The inference bundle is conditional on membership in the common-envelope finite-attractor class; this premise establishes neither Guo--Xu membership nor an applied recursion certification, and caps the positioning at field tier.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 5.14 proves a fixed-horizon realized-quadratic-variation studentized statistic converges to N(0,1) without deterministic variance stabilization, under martingale, moment, and variance-growth assumptions.
Theorems 3.2--3.3 give single-arm and joint deterministic Gaussian IPW-Z limits under scaled inverse-propensity convergence, with a consistent sandwich in Proposition 3.4.
The paper introduces directional stability, states that it is weaker than full-matrix stability, and derives normal and efficient inference under predictable-QV stabilization.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF pp. 8--13, Proposition 2.6, Theorem 2.7, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For Gaussian Thompson sampling, the multiple-optimal-arm pull/noise limit is governed by a unique SDE invariant law; the paper supplies non-Gaussian-limit confidence intervals rather than a finite-tail-attractor IPW-Z theorem.
The article studies a stochastic-approximation recursion with finitely many possible limit points and lower-bounds convergence probability to a prescribed point in its attraction domain.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Remove or derive the redundant p_-, omega_+, and h_+ restrictions, and state exactly which remaining primitive constants determine each uniform error bound.

Replace the generic uniformization claim over Saco with an explicit finite-T Berry--Esseen or coverage-error bound depending on the basin-attraction modulus, thereby making the recursion-level advance more than a repackaging of self-normalization.

Resolve the bounded Guo--Xu dynamics question for a nontrivial compact initial-state region and use that certified recursion as a worked member of the inference class after separately defining its causal score and target.

recommended_next_step: Revise the law class to a minimal primitive assumption set, then sharpen the direct Saco comparison with a quantitative recursion-derived guarantee before advancing to Stage 0.
